title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 432
paragraphs: So recalling this, he said in anger to Prexaspes: “Learn then for yourself now whether the Persians speak the truth, or whether, when they say this, it is they themselves who are out of their senses. For if I, shooting at your son there standing before the entrance of the chamber, hit him in the very middle of the heart, the Persians will be shown to be speaking falsely; but if I miss, then you may say the Persians are speaking truly and that I am not in my right mind.” Having said this, he drew his bow and hit the boy; and when the boy had fallen down, it is said that he ordered them to cut open his body and examine the place where he was hit, and as the arrow was found to be stuck in the heart, he laughed and was delighted, and said to the boy's father: “Prexaspes, it has now been made clear, as you see, that I am not mad, but that it is the Persians who are out of their senses; and now tell me: whom of all men did you ever see before this time hit the mark so well in shooting?” Then Prexaspes, seeing that the man was not in his right senses and fearing for himself, said: “Master, I think that not even God himself could have hit the mark so fairly.” Thus he acted at that time. On another occasion he condemned twelve Persians, men equal to the best, on a trivial charge, and buried them alive head downward.
